Advisory committee considering recommendation to do away with single-family zoning

Seattle Times obtained a leak draft of an advisory committee's recommendation to do away with single-family zoning. It's just a draft and nobody has to listen to the advisory committee's recommendations but I'm sure this will stir up some controversy. Personally I think it's the right call. There's no way to sustain Seattle's growth and keep rent/housing prices affordable for a large majority of the city without dramatically increasing our housing density but I'm not home owner and I'm sure they feel differently.

What are other people's thoughts?

I do own a small townhome (all I could afford, houses are way too expensive), so I'm already used to multi-tenant properties. The only issue I would take with this proposal is that they mention the possibility of not extending this to all areas of the city. This implies that certain areas would remain single family homes. Kind of seems like one could cherry pick this for their own purposes.

We can still be a city for everyone, but only if we give up our outdated ideal of every family living in their own home on a 5,000 square foot lot,” a draft letter from the committee co-chairs reads.

The mentality of this is staggering. It's the dumbest idea I've heard in a long time. Poor people can't afford nice Single Family Homes so lets get rid of Single Family Homes....Really? Having your own home and a little room to stretch is 'outdated'???

SFZ is the primary feature that makes a neighborhood 'nice'. Basically they want to allow low income multi unit structures everywhere. This will spread the shitty multi unit stuff into the nice areas until there are no more nice areas. You'll still have the concentrated bad neighborhoods but you'll eliminate the concentrated nice neighborhoods.

I think there's obviously a shortage of neighborhoods zoned for multi family dwellings based on current demand for housing. Neighborhoods that I can't afford to live in aren't "nice" neighborhoods to me. Why not let the market decide and let developers build whatever will be worth the most value?
I believe they are not talking only of addressing a shortage, they are wholesale removing the category of SFH. I think that is drastic.

What are attitudes toward guns like in your country? Do you agree with the consensus? What do you wish was different about the way your country handles gun policy?
American here. We've got gun culture. It seems to be a major discussion point with people from other countries. What are cultural attitudes towards guns and gun ownership in your country?

Canada.

I honestly don't know what laws we have. I know a few years ago we tried a "long gun registry" but that was removed. We have somewhat similar crime compared to the US in the major cities, not nowhere near the scale of similar-sized cities (Toronto area is larger than Chicago, and there's a lot less gun-related events).

I don't know anyone personally who owns a handgun. I don't know anyone personally who owns an "assault rifle", regardless of the definition. I know people with hunting rifles and shotguns, the Great White North has a long history of that (and you need a decent rifle to take down a moose).
I assume you live in a big city? What is your perception of Americans and guns?

I currently live in a rural area, and the only city in my province has 45,000 people. We had a total of 11 gun releated crimes in 2012 for the entire province (population 135k).

I have previously lived in larger cities, but as an adult the only city was Ottawa. And even when I live there, I didn't know of a single person who owned a gun - not even hunting, since nobody I knew there really went out into the country.

My perception of America and guns... and I've been downvoted to oblivion for some observations from outside, but here is the major observation I have about America: nobody can talk about it. The people who are pro-gun, as soon as they hear anyone wanting to bring up gun control, will attack everyone who even tries to voice an opinion and discuss the matter openly. And they believe that the only option on the table is "take away our guns." Even with something as seemingly simple as registering a gun, "That just gives the government a list of gun owners!" Everything else needs to be registers: homes, vehicles, children... but not guns.

Do I think America is gun-obsessed? Yes.

Do I think America could help with gun violence with measured changes to gun laws? Yes.

Do I know what changes to suggest? No.

But... nobody can come up with suggestions, because the gun owners won't talk.

I'm from the UK. I think having such easy access to guns in the US makes it much easier for criminal activity. People say "but how will I defend myself from gun-toting criminals if I don't have a gun? If I gave up my guns, the criminals wouldn't." I'd say the following as a main rebuttal:

A criminal with intent, and a plan, will have drawn his gun on you first before you have a chance to get yours. Either you submit to being robbed, or you are shot.

It also forces police's hands in many cases - if a criminal reaches for a gun, you'd damn well better stop him from getting to it. With guns absolutely commonplace in America, it's always better to assume the suspect has a gun, leading to a LOT of police shootings. So much so that it's barely even a story any more. And it does not do to have your policemen, the people looking after your safety, to become so desensitized to taking life.

Guns are an unbelievably easy, effective and convenient way to take a life. Just squeeze the trigger, bang, and the guy's dead. It's distant and impersonal, and takes no time at all. I think all that contributes to the psyche of gun-owners, and as such, people tend to find it easier to take a life. This is a personal opinion of mine, and I don't know how it holds up if it were to be put under scientific scrutiny.

But for a quick-blast comparison, the murder rate in NYC is 5.6 murder victims per 100,000 people. The murder rate in London is 1.6 per 100,000 people. I believe (again, unprovable) that the prevalence of guns in your culture has an awful lot to do with that.

We have plenty of gangland areas, too - but far fewer guns. Our police don't even carry weapons except in special circumstances.

I realise that this comment hasn't really talked about gun attitudes in the UK. But that's because we don't really talk about it over here, because guns just aren't a part of our lives, and I see that as a positive thing. Guns for me represent a tool used only for violence and murder. It's not a pretty sight. When we do talk about it, we talk about the USA's attitude, usually because the news has come out of a gun murder or police shooting.

To play devil's advocate: All of our largest cities with high crime rates (NYC, Chicago, New Orleans, Detroit) have strict gun control... Do you think gun policy in the UK is good the way it is? What do you think should change?

I didn't realise that. To stay within NYC for the sake of simplicity - aren't all the gangbangers constantly boasting about owning guns? Not that it's necessarily true, but plenty of the US rappers from those big cities mention their gun at some point in damn near every song. Plus all the footage you see on WorldStar. I'm wondering if maybe those gun control policies aren't working.

I personally think it's great the way it is in the UK. I've never come across a gun in my life that wasn't wielded by a trained professional, and that's the way I'd like it to stay. There will, naturally, be people who want change, but as I've had no exposure to the ideas they present, I really can't voice my opinion on them.

In rural areas... there's not much need of a handgun. Even home protection is most likely to be a shotgun. People who hunt to hunt use a shotgun or a rifle. Handgun is next to useless trying to target shoot a deer, and why the hell would you need an AR-15?
